```{r}
library(httr)
library(xml2)
library(stringr)
```

# Question 1: How many Sars-Cov-2 papers?

```{r}
# Downloading the website
website <- xml2::read_html("https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=sars-cov-2")

# Finding the counts
counts <- xml2::xml_find_first(website, xpath = "/html/body/main/div[9]/div[2]/div[2]/div[1]/div[1]/h3/span")

# Turning it into text
counts <- as.character(counts)

# Extracting the data using regex
totalcount <- stringr::str_extract(counts, "[0-9,.]+")

# Removing any commas/dots so that we can convert to numeric
totalcount <- gsub('[,.]', '', totalcount)

totalcount <- as.numeric(totalcount)
print(totalcount)
```

## Summary

There are 278,150 papers about Sars-Cov-2.

# Question 2: Get article abstracts and author

```{r}
# read in text, each line is a separate character
abstracts <- readLines("C:/Users/nweit/Downloads/abstract-sars-cov-2-set.txt", warn = FALSE)
# combine all text into one character
abstracts <- paste(abstracts, collapse = '\n')
# split the text whenever 3 new lines occur in a row (indicating two blank lines)
abstracts <- unlist(strsplit(abstracts, split = '\n\n\n'))
# replace any remaining "\n" symbols with spaces
abstracts <- gsub("\n", " ", abstracts)
# replace multiple spaces with single space
abstracts <- gsub(" +", " ", abstracts)

length(abstracts)
head(abstracts,3)
```

# Question 3: Distribution of universities

What are the 10 most common institutions? Discuss how you could you improve these results.

```{r}
institution <- str_extract_all(
  abstracts,
  "([A-Z][A-Za-z'-]* ){1,10}University|University of( [A-Z][A-Za-z'-]*){1,10}|([A-Z][A-Za-z'-]* ){1,10}Institute of( [A-Z][A-Za-z'-]*){1,10}"
  ) 
institution <- unlist(institution)
table(institution)

head(sort(table(institution), decreasing = TRUE), 10)
```

## Summary

The 10 most common institutions, in order from most to least common are: University of California (4,358), Stanford University (1,171), University of Southern California (786), University of San Francisco (701), University of California San Diego (682), The University (398), University of Washington (338), Columbia University (274), University of California Los Angeles (254), and Johns Hopkins University (246). The results can be improved by expanding the list of terms to extract. This script returned "The University" in the top ten most common institutions, so modifying the regular expression to make "The" optional in the pattern would return a different school in place of "The University." Expanding the expression to include other names for institutions, such as "College," would also produce better results. Another way to improve the results would be to decide whether to combine or separate universities with similar names. For example, "University of California" may refer to UC Davis or UC Berkeley. As the third abstract above this code chunk shows, UC Davis is written as "University of California-Davis." From my understanding, the hyphen is not included in the regular expression, and operating on the assumption that UC Berkeley is written as "University of California-Berkeley," then the regular expression will combine the two schools as "University of California."

# Question 4: Make a tidy dataset

```{r}
# read in text, each line is a separate character
abstracts <- readLines("C:/Users/nweit/Downloads/abstract-sars-cov-2-set.txt", warn = FALSE)
# combine all text into one character
abstracts <- paste(abstracts, collapse = '\n')
# split the text whenever 3 new lines occur in a row (indicating two blank lines)
abstracts <- unlist(strsplit(abstracts, split = '\n\n\n'))

# Extract the journal title for each article
journal <- str_extract(abstracts, "(?<=\\. )[^\\n]+")

# Extract the title of each article
titles <- sapply(abstracts, function(x){
  unlist(strsplit(x, split = "\n\n"))[2]
}, USE.NAMES = FALSE)

# Extract the authors of each article
authors <- sapply(abstracts, function(x){
  unlist(strsplit(x, split = "\n\n"))[3]
}, USE.NAMES = FALSE)

# Extract author affiliations for each abstract
affiliations <- str_extract(abstracts, "(?<=\\n\\nAuthor information:\\n)[\\s\\S]*?(?=\\n\\n)")

# Data Frame
papers <- data.frame(
  Journal = journal, 
  Title = titles, 
  Authors = authors, 
  Affiliations = affiliations
  )
knitr::kable(papers[1:5, ], format = "html")

```

I added 'format = "html"' to knitr::kable(papers[1:5, ]) because the formatting was getting messed up when rendering.
